atoms.text: This guide describes how to let the Tessera Batch worker role read raw order files and write curated output in an S3 bucket. The role tessera-batch-role and the bucket acme-orders-data both belong to account 111122223333. Because they share an account, the grant is carried entirely by the role's identity-based policy in IAM. Attach a policy to tessera-batch-role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-data/raw/orders/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-data/curated/orders/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-data with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/orders/. Do not edit the bucket policy; it stays unchanged and does not mention the role. Configure the job to read CSV files from raw/orders/ and write Parquet files to curated/orders/. To verify, run a test job and confirm that new objects appear under curated/orders/ and that the access log shows tessera-batch-role as the requester.

This guide describes how to let the Tessera Batch worker role read raw order files and write curated output in an S3 bucket. The role tessera-batch-role belongs to account 111122223333, while the bucket acme-orders-data is owned by a different account, 444455556666. Because access crosses an account boundary, the grant is carried by a statement that the bucket owner adds to the bucket policy. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/tessera-batch-role. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-data/raw/orders/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-data/curated/orders/*, plus s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/orders/. Configure the job to read CSV files from raw/orders/ and write Parquet files to curated/orders/. To verify, run a test job and confirm that new objects appear under curated/orders/ and that the access log shows tessera-batch-role as the requester from account 111122223333.

This guide explains how to give the QuerySpan execution role access to a clickstream dataset and a results location in an S3 bucket. The role queryspan-exec-role and the bucket acme-warehouse are in the same account, 111122223333. Access is granted only through the identity-based policy attached to the role in IAM. That policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/clickstream/* so the engine can scan Parquet partitions. It also allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/query-results/*, where result files are written. Add s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN so the engine can enumerate partitions. The bucket policy is not changed. After saving the policy, run a SELECT statement and confirm that a result file appears under query-results/ with the role recorded as the writer.

This guide explains how to give the QuerySpan execution role access to a clickstream dataset and a results location in an S3 bucket. The role queryspan-exec-role belongs to account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-warehouse is owned by a different account, 444455556666. The bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy. The statement names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/queryspan-exec-role as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/clickstream/* so the engine can scan Parquet partitions. It also allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/query-results/*, where result files are written. A second action list allows s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN. After the owner saves the policy, run a SELECT statement and confirm that a result file appears under query-results/ with the cross-account role recorded as the writer.

This guide covers permissions for the Streamline Ingest consumer, which reads newly landed JSON files and writes progress checkpoints. The consumer runs as streamline-reader-role in account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-landing is in that same account. The grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy; the bucket policy is left as it is. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-landing/landing/events/* so the consumer can read incoming files. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-landing/checkpoints/streamline/* so it can persist and reload offsets. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-landing restricted to the landing/events/ and checkpoints/streamline/ prefixes. Set the consumer's source path to landing/events/ and its checkpoint path to checkpoints/streamline/. Start the consumer and confirm that checkpoint objects are updated after each processed batch.

This guide covers permissions for the Streamline Ingest consumer, which reads newly landed JSON files and writes progress checkpoints. The consumer runs as streamline-reader-role in account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-landing is owned by a different account, 444455556666. The grant is made by the bucket owner through a statement added to the bucket policy. The statement uses arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/streamline-reader-role as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-landing/landing/events/* so the consumer can read incoming files. It allows s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-landing/checkpoints/streamline/* so the consumer can persist and reload offsets. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to the landing/events/ and checkpoints/streamline/ prefixes. Set the consumer's source path to landing/events/ and its checkpoint path to checkpoints/streamline/, then start it and confirm that checkpoint objects are updated after each processed batch.

This guide shows how to authorize the LogFold runner to aggregate application logs stored in an S3 bucket. The runner assumes logfold-runner-role, and both the role and the bucket acme-logs are in account 111122223333. Access is provided only by the role's identity-based policy in IAM. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs/logs/app/* so the runner can read gzip-compressed log files. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs/rollups/hourly/* so it can write hourly rollup files. Include s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs with a prefix condition of logs/app/. No change is made to the bucket policy. Schedule the job hourly with input logs/app/ and output rollups/hourly/, then check that one rollup object is created for each completed hour.

The runner assumes logfold-runner-role in account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-logs is owned by a different account, 444455556666. Access is provided by a statement that the bucket owner adds to the bucket policy. The statement lists arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/logfold-runner-role as the Principal. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs/logs/app/* so the runner can read gzip-compressed log files. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs/rollups/hourly/* so the runner can write hourly rollup files. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of logs/app/. Schedule the job hourly with input logs/app/ and output rollups/hourly/, then check that one rollup object is created for each completed hour.

This guide describes how to let the FeatureLoom job role build feature snapshots from event partitions in an S3 bucket. The role featureloom-job-role and the bucket acme-ml-data are both in account 111122223333. The permissions are defined only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not modified. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ml-data/events/* so the job can read date-partitioned event files. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ml-data/features/snapshots/* for the snapshot output. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ml-data with an s3:prefix condition covering events/. Configure the job to read partitions named dt=YYYY-MM-DD and to write one snapshot directory per run date. Run the job for a single date and confirm that the snapshot appears under features/snapshots/ with the expected partition name.

This guide explains how to grant the Ledgerline report service access to daily warehouse exports and a monthly report location. The service runs as ledgerline-report-role in account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-finance-data belongs to the same account. The only policy that grants access is the identity-based policy on the role. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/exports/daily/* to read CSV export files. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data/reports/monthly/* to write the generated report files. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-data with an s3:prefix condition of exports/daily/. The bucket policy is left untouched. Set the report job to read one month of exports and write a single consolidated CSV to reports/monthly/, and confirm that the file is present after the first scheduled run.

This guide covers access for the Sieve Validate service, which checks incoming data files and writes validation output. The service uses sieve-validator-role in account 111122223333, and the bucket acme-intake is in the same account. Access is granted solely through the role's identity-based policy in IAM. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake/incoming/* so the validator can read files awaiting checks. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake/validation-reports/* for JSON summaries, and on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake/quarantine/* for records that fail validation. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake with an s3:prefix condition of incoming/. The bucket policy is not changed. Run the validatoron a sample file containing malformed rows and confirm that a report appears in validation-reports/ and the rejected rows appear in quarantine/.

It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake/validation-reports/* for JSON summaries, and on arn:aws:s3:::acme-intake/quarantine/* for records that fail validation. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of incoming/. Run the validator on a sample file containing malformed rows and confirm that a report appears in validation-reports/ and the rejected rows appear in quarantine/.

This guide describes how to permit the MergeKit compactor to combine small ingest files into larger ones in an S3 bucket. The compactor runs as mergekit-compactor-role, and both that role and the bucket acme-ingest are in account 111122223333. Access is given only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy does not change. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest/ingest/small/* so the compactor can read the source files. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest/ingest/compacted/* for the merged output. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest with an s3:prefix condition of ingest/small/. Configure the compactor with a target file size of 256 MB, reading from ingest/small/ and writing to ingest/compacted/. Run it against one partition and confirm that the merged objects appear under ingest/compacted/ at the expected size.
